description: This topic explains evaporation and how it differs from boiling, the factors that affect evaporation and cooling, saturated and unsaturated vapour, humidity and dew point, the formation of dew, mist, fog, clouds and rain, and how humidity is measured and felt in everyday Tanzanian weather.

mcq.questionText: Evaporation is best described as the change of a liquid into vapour that takes place:

options.text: only at the boiling point throughout the whole liquid
at any temperature and only from the surface of the liquid
only when the liquid is heated by a flame
only inside bubbles formed at the bottom of the liquid

mcq.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid at any temperature, unlike boiling which occurs throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is a difference between boiling and evaporation?

options.text: Boiling happens only at the surface while evaporation happens throughout
Boiling happens at a fixed temperature while evaporation happens at any temperature
Boiling needs no heat while evaporation needs heat
Boiling occurs only in liquids while evaporation occurs only in solids

mcq.explanation: Boiling occurs at a definite boiling point throughout the liquid, while evaporation occurs from the surface at any temperature below boiling.

mcq.questionText: Which change will increase the rate of evaporation of water from an open dish?

options.text: Lowering the temperature of the water
Increasing the surface area of the water
Increasing the humidity of the surrounding air
Covering the dish with a tight lid

mcq.explanation: A larger surface area allows more molecules to escape, so a wider, shallower dish evaporates faster.

mcq.questionText: Evaporation causes cooling of the remaining liquid because:

options.text: the fastest, most energetic molecules escape, leaving slower ones behind
the slowest molecules escape, leaving faster ones behind
heat is added to the liquid as molecules leave
the liquid gains molecules from the air

mcq.explanation: The molecules with the most kinetic energy escape during evaporation, lowering the average energy and therefore the temperature of the liquid left behind.

mcq.questionText: A wind blowing over wet clothes makes them dry faster mainly because it:

options.text: raises the boiling point of the water
removes saturated air near the clothes and replaces it with drier air
increases the humidity around the clothes
lowers the surface area of the clothes

mcq.explanation: Moving air carries away the moist air collecting above the clothes, allowing more water molecules to escape and speeding up evaporation.

mcq.questionText: A vapour is said to be saturated when:

options.text: it can still hold much more vapour at that temperature
it is in equilibrium with its liquid and can hold no more vapour at that temperature
it contains no water vapour at all
its temperature is always above the boiling point

mcq.explanation: Saturated vapour exists in equilibrium with its liquid, with as many molecules condensing as evaporating, so the air holds the maximum possible vapour at that temperature.

options.text: the total mass of water vapour in the air
the ratio of the actual vapour present to the vapour needed to saturate the air at the same temperature
the temperature at which dew forms
the mass of water vapour per unit volume of air

mcq.explanation: Relative humidity compares the water vapour actually present with the amount needed to saturate the air at the same temperature, usually expressed as a percentage.

mcq.questionText: The dew point is the temperature at which:

options.text: water begins to boil
the air becomes saturated and water vapour starts to condense
ice begins to melt
all the water vapour leaves the air

mcq.explanation: When air is cooled to its dew point it becomes saturated, and any further cooling causes the excess vapour to condense as dew or droplets.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is commonly used to measure the relative humidity of the air?

options.text: Barometer
Hygrometer
Ammeter
Hydrometer

mcq.explanation: A hygrometer measures humidity. The wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer is a common type. A hydrometer (different word) measures liquid density.

mcq.questionText: In a wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer, a large difference between the two thermometer readings indicates that the air is:

options.text: very dry (low humidity)
fully saturated
exactly at its dew point
at 100% relative humidity

mcq.explanation: Dry air causes fast evaporation from the wet bulb, cooling it strongly, so a large gap between the bulbs means low humidity.

options.text: warm moist air rises, cools and the vapour condenses into tiny droplets
dry air sinks and warms up near the ground
water vapour is heated above its boiling point
rain freezes directly into solid ice on the ground

mcq.explanation: Rising warm moist air cools with height until it reaches its dew point, and the vapour condenses on dust particles to form the tiny droplets of a cloud.

mcq.questionText: Fog and mist are basically the same phenomenon as clouds except that they:

options.text: form high in the sky
form close to the ground
are made of dry dust only
are made of frozen ice crystals only

mcq.explanation: Mist and fog are tiny condensed water droplets formed near ground level when air close to the surface cools to its dew point.

mcq.questionText: Dew forms on grass in the early morning because the grass:

options.text: becomes warmer than the air at night
cools at night below the dew point, so vapour condenses on it
absorbs water from the soil through its roots
produces water vapour from inside the leaves

mcq.explanation: At night surfaces such as grass lose heat and cool below the dew point of the surrounding air, causing water vapour to condense onto them as dew.

mcq.questionText: On a hot, very humid day in Dar es Salaam people feel uncomfortable mainly because:

options.text: the air pressure is too low to breathe
high humidity slows the evaporation of sweat, reducing cooling of the body
sweat stops being produced by the body
the body absorbs water from the humid air

mcq.explanation: When the air is already moist, sweat evaporates slowly, so the body is cooled less and feels hot and sticky.

mcq.questionText: Absolute humidity is best described as:

options.text: the mass of water vapour present in a given volume of air
the temperature at which dew forms
the percentage of saturation of the air
the pressure of the dry air alone

mcq.explanation: Absolute humidity is the actual mass of water vapour in a given volume of air, often measured in grams per cubic metre.

fib.questionText: The escape of liquid molecules into vapour from the surface of a liquid at any temperature is called _____.
fib.explanation: Evaporation takes place at the surface of a liquid at any temperature, while boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature.

fib.questionText: Unlike evaporation, boiling takes place at a fixed temperature called the _____.
fib.explanation: Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at the definite boiling point, whereas evaporation can occur at any temperature.

fib.questionText: Increasing the _____ area of a liquid increases its rate of evaporation.
fib.explanation: A larger exposed surface area lets more molecules escape, so evaporation is faster.

fib.questionText: Because the most energetic molecules escape during evaporation, the liquid left behind becomes _____.
fib.explanation: Loss of the fastest molecules lowers the average kinetic energy of the remaining liquid, so its temperature falls.

fib.questionText: Air that contains the maximum amount of water vapour it can hold at a given temperature is said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Saturated air is in equilibrium with the liquid and can hold no more vapour at that temperature.

fib.questionText: The ratio of the water vapour actually present to the amount needed to saturate the air at the same temperature, expressed as a percentage, is the _____ humidity.
fib.explanation: Relative humidity compares the actual vapour content with the saturation amount at the same temperature.

fib.questionText: The temperature at which air becomes saturated and water vapour begins to condense is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Cooling air to its dew point makes it saturated, and further cooling causes condensation as dew or droplets.

fib.questionText: Tiny water droplets that condense near the ground and reduce visibility form _____ (or mist).
fib.explanation: Fog and mist are condensed droplets formed close to the ground when surface air cools to its dew point.

fib.questionText: An instrument used to measure the humidity of the air is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A hygrometer measures humidity; the wet-and-dry bulb type is widely used.

fib.questionText: In a wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer, the wet bulb usually reads a _____ temperature than the dry bulb because of evaporation.
fib.explanation: Evaporation of water from the wet bulb cools it, so it reads a lower temperature than the dry bulb unless the air is fully saturated.

tf.questionText: Evaporation can take place at any temperature, not only at the boiling point.
tf.explanation: Evaporation occurs from the surface of a liquid at any temperature, while boiling needs the boiling point.

tf.questionText: Boiling takes place only at the surface of a liquid.
tf.explanation: Boiling takes place throughout the whole liquid with bubbles forming inside it; it is evaporation that happens only at the surface.

tf.questionText: Increasing the humidity of the surrounding air slows down the rate of evaporation.
tf.explanation: Moist air is already close to saturation, so fewer molecules can escape and evaporation is slower.

tf.questionText: Evaporation warms up the liquid that is left behind.
tf.explanation: Evaporation causes cooling because the most energetic molecules escape, lowering the temperature of the remaining liquid.

tf.questionText: Saturated air holds the maximum amount of water vapour possible at that temperature.
tf.explanation: When air is saturated it is in equilibrium with the liquid and cannot hold any more vapour at that temperature.

tf.questionText: Relative humidity of 100% means the air is completely dry.
tf.explanation: 100% relative humidity means the air is fully saturated with water vapour, not dry.

tf.questionText: Clouds, mist and fog are all formed by the condensation of water vapour into tiny droplets.
tf.explanation: All three form when moist air cools to its dew point and the vapour condenses; clouds form high up while mist and fog form near the ground.

tf.questionText: Dew forms when surfaces such as grass warm up above the temperature of the surrounding air at night.
tf.explanation: Dew forms when surfaces cool below the dew point at night, causing vapour to condense on them.

tf.questionText: On a humid day sweat evaporates slowly, so the body is cooled less and feels hotter.
tf.explanation: High humidity slows the evaporation of sweat, reducing the cooling effect and making people feel uncomfortable.

tf.questionText: Clothes dry faster on a hot, windy day with low humidity than on a cool, still, humid day.
tf.explanation: Higher temperature, wind and low humidity all increase the rate of evaporation, so clothes dry faster under those conditions.

summary.questionText: State two differences between evaporation and boiling.
summary.correctAnswer: Evaporation occurs at the surface at any temperature, while boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a fixed boiling point.
summary.explanation: Evaporation is a surface process happening at any temperature; boiling is a bulk process happening at the definite boiling point.

summary.questionText: List four factors that increase the rate of evaporation of a liquid.
summary.correctAnswer: Higher temperature, larger surface area, more air movement (wind), and lower humidity of the surrounding air.
summary.explanation: These factors help more molecules escape from the surface, speeding up evaporation.

summary.questionText: Explain why evaporation produces a cooling effect.
summary.correctAnswer: The fastest, most energetic molecules escape from the surface, lowering the average kinetic energy and so the temperature of the liquid left behind.
summary.explanation: Loss of high-energy molecules reduces the average energy of the remaining liquid, cooling it.

summary.questionText: What is meant by saturated vapour?
summary.correctAnswer: Vapour that is in equilibrium with its liquid, where the air holds the maximum vapour possible at that temperature.
summary.explanation: In saturated air the rates of evaporation and condensation are equal, so no more vapour can be added at that temperature.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between absolute humidity and relative humidity.
summary.correctAnswer: Absolute humidity is the actual mass of water vapour per unit volume of air; relative humidity is the ratio of actual vapour to the saturation amount at the same temperature, as a percentage.
summary.explanation: Absolute humidity gives an amount, while relative humidity gives a percentage comparison with saturation.

summary.questionText: Define the dew point of air.
summary.correctAnswer: The temperature at which the air becomes saturated and water vapour in it begins to condense.
summary.explanation: Cooling air to its dew point makes it saturated; further cooling causes condensation.

summary.questionText: Describe briefly how clouds and rain are formed.
summary.correctAnswer: Warm moist air rises and cools to its dew point, vapour condenses into tiny droplets forming clouds; when droplets join and grow heavy they fall as rain.
summary.explanation: Condensation of cooled rising air forms clouds, and the coalescing droplets eventually fall as rain.

summary.questionText: Explain how a wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer measures humidity.
summary.correctAnswer: Water evaporates from the wet bulb and cools it; the difference between the dry and wet bulb readings is used with a table to find the relative humidity. A bigger difference means drier air.
summary.explanation: The amount of cooling of the wet bulb depends on how fast water evaporates, which depends on the humidity.

summary.questionText: Give two effects of high humidity on daily life.
summary.correctAnswer: It makes people feel hot and uncomfortable because sweat evaporates slowly, and it makes clothes take longer to dry.
summary.explanation: High humidity slows evaporation, reducing body cooling and delaying drying of clothes.

summary.questionText: Why do coastal towns such as Dar es Salaam and Tanga usually feel more humid than inland towns?
summary.correctAnswer: They are near the sea, so there is a lot of evaporation of sea water adding water vapour to the air, raising the humidity.
summary.explanation: Large bodies of water near the coast supply plenty of water vapour, increasing humidity compared with drier inland areas.

hoq.questionText: A nurse rubs spirit (a volatile liquid) on a patient's skin and the skin feels very cold. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: The spirit warms the skin by adding heat as it spreads
The spirit evaporates quickly, taking heat from the skin and cooling it
The spirit freezes instantly on the skin
The spirit increases the humidity of the skin so it feels cold

hoq.explanation: A volatile liquid evaporates rapidly, and the energy needed for evaporation is drawn from the skin, producing a strong cooling sensation.

hoq.questionText: Two identical wet shirts are hung out at the same time. Shirt X is spread wide open in a breezy, sunny spot; shirt Y is folded and left in a still, shaded, humid corner. Which shirt dries first and why?

options.text: Shirt Y, because shade and humidity speed up evaporation
Both dry at exactly the same rate because they are identical
Shirt X, because larger surface area, warmth, wind and lower humidity all increase evaporation
Shirt Y, because folding increases its surface area

hoq.explanation: Shirt X experiences higher temperature, greater exposed surface area, moving air and drier surroundings, all of which speed up evaporation, so it dries first.

hoq.questionText: On a clear, calm night the dry bulb of a hygrometer reads 24 C and the wet bulb reads 18 C. Towards dawn the air temperature falls to 18 C. What is most likely to happen?

options.text: Nothing, because the air can never become saturated
The air, now cooled close to its dew point, becomes saturated and dew or mist forms
The water on surfaces boils away
The humidity drops to zero and the air becomes very dry

hoq.explanation: The wet-and-dry readings indicate the air is fairly moist; as the temperature falls towards the dew point the air saturates, so excess vapour condenses as dew or mist.
